claims.text: Dose (IV): 0.1–0.2 mg/kg every 4 hours as needed, at the lowest dose that gives adequate analgesia;
claims.quote: Initiate treatment with Morphine Sulfate Injection in adults at a dosing range of 0.1 mg to 0.2 mg per kg every 4 hours as needed to manage pain, and at the lowest dose necessary to achieve adequate analgesia.

claims.text: inject slowly (rapid IV may cause chest wall rigidity).
claims.quote: Morphine must be injected slowly; rapid intravenous administration may result in chest wall rigidity.

claims.text: MAOI use now or within the last 14 days;
claims.quote: Concurrent use of monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) or use of MAOIs within the last 14 days

claims.text: known or suspected GI obstruction, including paralytic ileus.
claims.quote: Known or suspected gastrointestinal obstruction, including paralytic ileus

claims.text: Interactions: benzodiazepines or other CNS depressants (including alcohol) may cause profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma and death.
claims.quote: Concomitant use of opioids with benzodiazepines or other central nervous system (CNS) depressants, including alcohol, may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death.
claims.locator: WARNING: SERIOUS AND LIFE-THREATENING RISKS FROM USE OF MORPHINE SULFATE INJECTION

claims.text: Monitor closely for respiratory depression, especially at the start or after a dose increase;
claims.quote: Serious, life-threatening, or fatal respiratory depression may occur. Monitor closely, especially upon initiation or following a dosage increase.

claims.text: have naloxone and resuscitative equipment immediately available.
claims.quote: Have naloxone injection and resuscitative equipment immediately available.

claims.text: Overdose: respiratory depression, somnolence progressing to stupor or coma, constricted pupils, bradycardia, hypotension;
claims.quote: Acute overdose with morphine can be manifested by respiratory depression, somnolence progressing to stupor or coma, skeletal muscle flaccidity, cold and clammy skin, constricted pupils, and, in some cases, pulmonary edema, bradycardia, hypotension
For clinically significant respiratory or circulatory depression secondary to morphine overdose, administer an opioid overdose reversal agent such as naloxone or nalmefene.

claims.text: and monitor until spontaneous breathing is reliably back, because reversal is shorter than morphine's action.
claims.quote: Because the duration of opioid reversal is expected to be less than the duration of action of morphine in Morphine Sulfate Injection, carefully monitor the patient until spontaneous respiration is reliably reestablished.
